collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Raiders demand food in return for leaving the village alone: pay them, or refuse and prepare.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A raider has stood on the reef and shouted the demand: twenty baskets of food every moon, and the village will be left in peace. Otherwise, they will come. (subject) says twenty baskets is a price worth paying for peace. (friend) says pay once, and they will never stop asking. What should the village do?

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village pays. The raiders take the baskets and go. The next moon, they come again, and the moon after that. It is a hungry season. But nobody is hurt, and (subject) says that is worth a great deal. (friend) starts quietly training more warriors.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village refuses. For a month, everyone waits, watches and drills. The raiders come once, at night, see the whole village waiting on the beach with torches, and do not land. They never ask again.
